measures: Whether the resume evidences measuring model quality with something that could have returned a negative answer.
source: Criteria drafted for ticket 11 against the category 04 defined and the 5/6 evidence 02 recorded (inventory.md section 5). Wording drawn from the baseline run: both judges, unprompted, reached for evaluation methodology, benchmark provenance, baselines, eval set and measurement method (baseline-agreement.md, findings-identity.md section 2).

criteria.name: a measurement happened
criteria.question: Does any bullet say the quality of a model or its output was measured -- an eval, a benchmark, a test set, an A/B test, human annotation, a quality metric?
criteria.yes_requires: A quote naming the act of measuring. The measurement may be crude; this criterion only asks that one exists.
criteria.no_looks_like: Every bullet stops at building or shipping: 'Fine-tuned a classifier', 'built a RAG pipeline' -- nothing says anyone checked whether it worked. Serving numbers are not a quality measurement either: latency, throughput, cost and uptime say how the system ran, not whether its answers were any good, and Production ownership's C3 already asks for those.

criteria.name: named metric and number
criteria.question: Is the measurement stated as a named metric with a number?
criteria.yes_requires: A metric a reader could recompute and the value it took -- 'F1 0.82', 'pass@1 from 41% to 63%', 'p95 hallucination rate under 2%'.
criteria.no_looks_like: 'Improved model quality', 'strong benchmark results', 'high accuracy'. Also a number attached to something other than quality -- a token count, a dataset size, a GPU count -- standing in for a result.

criteria.name: what it was run on
criteria.question: Does the resume say what the measurement was run on?
criteria.yes_requires: A named dataset, a held-out or golden set, a stated number of annotated examples, production traffic, or named human raters -- the provenance of the number, not only its value.
criteria.no_looks_like: A metric with no subject. 'Hit 92% accuracy' -- on what, chosen how, how many examples.

criteria.name: compared to something
criteria.question: Is the number compared with something -- a baseline, a prior model, a before and after, a target?
criteria.yes_requires: The other end of the comparison, named: the model or method that was beaten, the previous value, the bar that had to be cleared.
criteria.no_looks_like: A single standalone number. '0.87 F1' is unreadable without knowing what 0.87 replaced or beat.

criteria.name: could have returned a negative answer
criteria.question: Does any bullet show the measurement was capable of coming back bad -- and say what happened when it did?
criteria.yes_requires: A regression caught, a failure mode found, a model or approach rejected on the numbers, a launch gated or blocked, an eval that ran on every change. fluidstack's bar: an eval that told you the truth about model quality before users did.
criteria.no_looks_like: Every number is a win. The evals appear only where they confirmed the work, and nothing was ever turned down because of one.

bands.label: E
bands.name: Nothing measured
bands.reads: Nothing in the resume says anyone checked whether the work was any good.

bands.label: D
bands.name: Measured, not reported
bands.rule: C1 met, and either C2 unmet or neither C3 nor C4 met
bands.reads: Evaluation is claimed, but no metric and number arrive, or the number stands alone with nothing behind or beside it.

bands.label: C
bands.name: A number
bands.rule: C1 and C2 met, and exactly one of C3, C4
bands.reads: A named metric with a value, and half of what makes it readable -- what it ran on, or what it beat, not both.

bands.label: B
bands.name: A readable result
bands.rule: C1, C2, C3 and C4 met, C5 unmet
bands.reads: The number, its subject and its comparison are all present -- and every measurement in the resume came back a win.

bands.label: A
bands.name: Evaluation that could say no
bands.reads: The resume shows a measurement that was allowed to fail, and what changed when it did.
